purpose: Quarantine a public SEC MIDAS market-structure state for source publication-lag and PIT feasibility before any performance evaluation.

external_basis.source: U.S. SEC Market Structure Data Downloads / MIDAS
external_basis.observation: The SEC publishes individual-security market-structure metrics, including cancel-to-trade ratio, trade-to-order volume, hidden rate/volume and odd-lot rate/volume; the current public downloads are updated through June 2026.

The source methodology explicitly describes a monthly CRSP universe update with a 3-4 week lag from the prior month's final trading day, making publication timing a first-order PIT question. It also documents that the SEC round-lot definition changed starting November 3, 2025, so odd-lot-derived measures cannot be treated as a single-regime series across that boundary.

candidates.name: SEC MIDAS Market-Friction State
candidates.hypothesis: A frozen public market-structure state built from order cancellation, trade-to-order, hidden-volume and odd-lot activity may capture a distinct trading-friction/market-participation regime that is not reducible to daily price momentum or volatility.
candidates.construction: Use only the SEC's published individual-security market-structure fields available at the verified publication cutoff. Treat the source release date as part of the state. Derive a predeclared non-fitted state from the published fields; no daily signal is allowed unless historical publication dates are independently reconstructible.
pit_requirements: field-definition and round-lot regime change handling
candidates.next_gate: historical publication-lag and individual-security archive audit

notes: Q125 is discovery design only and contains no project performance evidence.
The SEC documentation says the CRSP universe is updated monthly with a 3-4 week lag; this must be incorporated into the public-availability clock rather than assumed away.
The candidate is deliberately not formulated as a higher-frequency order-flow signal because the public SEC download cadence may be too slow for that interpretation.

The November 3, 2025 round-lot definition change is a mandatory regime boundary for any odd-lot-derived feature; no pooled pre/post-series interpretation is permitted before a definition-consistency audit.
No ranking, selection, tuning, holdout use, performance authorization, promotion or live execution is permitted.
